means: CGI - geometry lit by a renderer, with specular highlights, ambient occlusion and perspective-correct surfaces. What a game engine or Blender produces.
does: In the positive it plasticises faces and hair and destroys the keyline. In the NEGATIVE it is genuinely useful on this checkpoint, because SDXL anime models drift toward glossy 3D-ish rendering on hair highlights and eyes when the prompt runs long. One practical note: the trained danbooru tag is the bare '3d', which is the form this project standing negative actually uses - write '3d', not '3d render', if you want it to bite.
reach_for_it: never in the positive. In the negative, always - it is one of the three medium tags this project keeps there permanently.
used_in: the standing negative in craft/ANIME_MODELS.md, as '3d'
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short dark hair, plain jacket, standing, city street, daytime
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
